summary:
Ah, Patrice; how many good things have happened since I last wrote you. I’ve really gotten back into writing; I sent off my doubleday novel at last, which I mainly wrote back in 1970 and never could seem to finish: FLOW MY TEARS, THE POLICEMAN SAID. I completely rewrote it in the final draft, adding all sorts of new touches. I had already done 9 revisions and thought it to be perfect. Well, I was wrong. It underwent much improvement. So far I haven’t heard from Doubleday—it’s too soon, yet—but I think they’ll like it. It’s a long novel, by the way: 295 pages rather than say 238 which MAZE OF DEATH was. Also, I wrote a new 6,000 word story for an anthology by Ed Ferman and Barry Malzberg. My first story since “The Electric Ant.” That was about five years ago. Also for Ed Ferman. I really consider this new story to be the best one I’ve ever done. 

How have you been? We’ve been trying to write to you, but in addition to doing the final on TEARS and the story I’ve been sick with double pneumonia and damn near died. I was sitting here at my typewriter with a temperature of 102, typing away. We didn’t have any money so I didn’t go to the doctor; I just sat up all night, night after night, so I could breathe. Both my lungs filled up. But I’m okay now. Tess took very good care of me.
